info.title: Youverify Cowork API
info.description:
Entity, Activity, Signal, Case and Workflow Events Management endpoints — the core Cowork platform object model. Assembled from doc.youverify.co/api-reference-sdk, endpoints kept in the exact order they appear in the GitBook navigation.

Account-wide error responses (401, 429, 500 on every endpoint; 402 on paid verification calls; 404 on lookup-by-ID calls) are sourced verbatim from Youverify's own "Youverify OS Error Codes" and "Response Codes" pages (doc.youverify.co/youverify-os-error-codes, /get-started/response-codes) and attached via components.responses, since those pages document them account-wide rather than per endpoint. Any error example that a specific endpoint's own page actually showed is kept exactly as documented there instead of being replaced by these.

tags.name: Entity Management
tags.description: Create, retrieve and verify entities (individuals or businesses) — the core object every check attaches to.

tags.name: Activity Management
tags.description: Inspect the verification activities run against your account.

tags.name: Signal Management
tags.description: Retrieve monitoring signals and their events, by entity or business.

tags.name: Case Management
tags.description: Create and manage compliance cases, including AI-generated case summaries.

tags.name: Workflow Events Management
tags.description: Send events to your Transaction Monitoring (TM) and Customer Onboarding (CO) workflows, and read the workflows and evaluations (runs) for your business.

ApiKeyAuth.name: token
ApiKeyAuth.description: Your Youverify API secret key. Never expose client-side.

Error401Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized — the token header is missing or invalid.

Error402PaymentRequired.description: Payment Required — your account balance is too low to run this check.

Error404NotFound.description: Not Found — the URL, or the resource ID in the URL, was not recognized.

Error429TooManyRequests.description: Too Many Requests — you have exceeded the rate limit; wait and retry.

Error500ServerError.description: Internal Server Error — a rare, unexpected failure on Youverify's side. Contact support@youverify.co if it persists.

Error503ServiceUnavailable.description: Service Unavailable — the upstream third-party data provider is currently unreachable.

eventType.description: The kind of event: transaction or account_activity (a login or a card event).

schemaVersion.description: Version of this payload schema. Only major version 1 is supported.

externalEventId.description: Your own unique id for this event. It is the idempotency key: sending the same id again returns the original evaluations instead of starting new ones.

eventStatus.description: Where the event is in its life. Only a triggering status starts a workflow (a transaction: acknowledged, pending; a login: attempted; a card event: requested, activated, pin_changed); any other status is stored and still updates the aggregates. Which statuses are allowed depends on the kind of event.

lifecycleId.description: Your identifier tying together several events that belong to the same lifecycle, for example one session or one payment.

metadata.description: Information about the event itself, the same on every event type. Any other key you add is kept and passed on.

source.description: The system the event came from, for example core-banking.

appVersion.description: The version of your app that sent the event.

traceId.description: A W3C trace id: 32 hex characters.

testMode.description: true evaluates and logs the event but never acts on it (no alerts, cases or shadow runs).

eventCategory.description: Routes the event to the workflows tagged with this category, for example finance or kyc.

data.description: The transaction: its payment type, amounts, parties and the flags you decide (isInternational, isNight).

paymentType.description: How the payment is made: its channel, rail, direction and instrument.

direction.description: Which way the money moves, relative to your business: OUTBOUND (you send) or INBOUND (you receive). It decides which party is your customer: the sender on OUTBOUND, the beneficiary on INBOUND.

channel.description: The routing key: CARD or TRANSFER.

rail.description: The payment scheme, for example NIP, RTGS, SWIFT, ACH, INTERNAL, WALLET, VISA, MASTERCARD, VERVE or AMEX. Extensible, so not an enum.

instrument.description: What kind of business event this is: CREDIT_TRANSFER, AUTHORISATION, REVERSAL, REFUND, CASH_WITHDRAWAL or ADVICE.

clearingSystem.description: The clearing or scheme operator (ISO 20022 code).

localInstrument.description: The scheme-specific product code (ISO 20022 code), for example NIP-INSTANT.

categoryPurpose.description: The category of purpose for the whole message (ISO 20022 code), for example SUPP, SALA or CASH.

financials.description: The money in the transaction: the total debited and its currency.

totalAmount.description: The total debited from the sender, greater than 0, as a number or a decimal string. It must equal the sum of the beneficiaries' transferDetails.amount. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of totalAmount: the debit currency.

totalBaseAmount.description: totalAmount converted to baseCurrency, as a number or a decimal string. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

baseCurrency.description: ISO 4217 house base currency used by threshold rules, typically USD.

exchangeRate.description: How many units of baseCurrency one unit of currency buys.

rateSource.description: Where the exchange rate came from, for example CBN.

rateTimestamp.description: When the exchange rate was captured (ISO 8601).

chargeBearer.description: Who pays the charges: DEBT (the sender), CRED (the beneficiary), SHAR (shared) or SLEV (service level).

parties.description: Who sends the money and who receives it.

entityId.description: Our id for the party. Send it whenever you have it: it skips the lookup.

entityType.description: What the party is: INDIVIDUAL or BUSINESS.

externalEntityId.description: Your own id for the party. Required when entityId is not sent.

name.description: The party's full legal name (up to 140 characters). Required when entityId is not sent.

accountNumber.description: The party's account number. Used to find or create the party when entityId is not sent, which is when it is required.

nationality.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 nationality; for a business, its country of incorporation.

countryOfResidence.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the party lives in.

placeOfBirth.description: Where the party was born (individuals only).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Required whenever an address is sent.

postCode.description: Postal or ZIP code (up to 16 characters).

countrySubdivision.description: State, province or region, for example LA for Lagos (up to 35 characters).

addressLines.description: Up to 7 free-text address lines of up to 70 characters each. Use only when you cannot send the structured fields above. string maxLength: 70]

scheme.description: The kind of identifier, for example BVN, NIN or PASSPORT.

issuerCountry.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country that issued it.

ultimateParty.description: The real originator or beneficiary, where different from this party. It is screened.

contact.description: How to reach the party. Used for link analysis only.

phone.description: The party's phone number, for example +2348012345678.

riskRating.description: Your own risk rating for the party, for example low, medium or high. Used as the customer's risk rating when we have none (variable Risk Rating).

accountAge.description: How long the account has been open, in the unit you give in accountAgeUnit. Send the two together. The Account Age variable holds whole years, so it is worked out as days ÷ 365, weeks ÷ 52 or months ÷ 12, rounded down.

accountAgeUnit.description: The unit accountAge is stated in: days, weeks, months or years. You choose it; send it with accountAge.

expectedMonthlyVolume.description: The transaction volume expected each month, declared or assigned at onboarding. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

accountStatus.description: The account's status: active, frozen, closed, suspended, restricted or dormant.

beneficialOwnerRiskTier.description: The highest risk tier among the beneficial owners or directors.

productLimit.description: The configured transaction and daily limit for the account or product. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

paymentItemId.description: Identifies this payment item: this beneficiary's share of the payment. Must be unique within the message when sent.

amount.description: Amount allocated to this beneficiary, in the debit currency (financials.currency). Greater than zero; the amounts of all beneficiaries must add up to financials.totalAmount. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of amount. Must equal financials.currency.

endToEndId.description: Optional. A reference the sender gives this payment item that stays the same through every bank and payment system it passes through, so the one payment can be traced end to end (ISO 20022 EndToEndId, up to 35 characters). For a card payment it is the retrieval reference number (RRN).

instructionId.description: Optional. Your own internal reference for this instruction (up to 35 characters). Unlike endToEndId, it is not passed on to other banks.

uetr.description: Optional. The unique end-to-end transaction reference: a UUID v4 that identifies one cross-border payment on the SWIFT network, the same for every bank on its route. Domestic payments, such as NIP, do not have one.

baseAmount.description: This item's amount converted to baseCurrency. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

baseCurrency.description: ISO 4217 house base currency of baseAmount, typically USD.

creditAmount.description: The amount the beneficiary receives in their own currency (creditCurrency), when a currency conversion applies. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

purposeCode.description: Why this payment is made (ISO External Purpose code), for example SUPP (supplier), SALA (salary) or TRAD (trade).

remittanceInfo.description: Free-text narrative or invoice reference for the payment (up to 140 characters).

isInternational.description: Optional. Whether the transaction crosses a border. You decide; the platform never works it out from the countries. When left out, the transaction is not treated as international.

isNight.description: Optional. Whether the transaction happened at night. You decide; the platform never works it out from the time. When left out, the transaction is not treated as a night transaction.

creationDateTime.description: When the transaction was created at the source (UTC, ISO 8601).

intermediaryBanks.description: Up to 3 intermediary banks the payment passes through, in order. They are screened. {

regulatoryReporting.description: Codes an authority requires you to report with the transaction. {

items.description: One reporting code for one authority.

authorityCountry.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the reporting authority.

detailsText.description: Free text (up to 35 characters per line).

isoRef.description: The ISO 20022 message the transaction maps to, for example pacs.008. Informational.

card.description: Card details. Required when paymentType.channel is CARD, and not allowed otherwise.

panToken.description: A token standing in for the card number. Never send the raw PAN.

bin.description: The first 6 to 8 digits of the card number (the bank identification number).

cardCountry.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country that issued the card.

entryMode.description: How the card was read: CHIP, CONTACTLESS, SWIPE, MANUAL, ECOM (online), TOKEN_WALLET or FALLBACK.

cvvResult.description: The result of the card security code check.

transmissionDateTime.description: When the message was transmitted (ISO 8583 field 7), ISO 8601.

cardholderPresent.description: Whether the cardholder was physically present.

isCrossBorder.description: Whether the card's country differs from the merchant's country.

threeDSecure.description: The 3-D Secure (online payment authentication) result. Required for ECOM.

status.description: The 3-D Secure outcome: Y authenticated, N failed, A attempted, U unavailable, R rejected.

eci.description: The two-digit electronic commerce indicator the card network returns, for example 05.

posConditionCode.description: Point-of-sale condition code: whether the card was present (ISO 8583 field 25).

status.description: Whether the transaction completed, is pending, or failed.

settled_at.description: When the transaction settled, if it has.

processed_at.description: When the platform received or processed the transaction.

fee_amount.description: The transaction fee, network fee, FX fee or service charge, as a number or a decimal string. In the currency's main unit, not its smallest one: naira, not kobo; dollars, not cents. Use decimals for the fraction, so 1500.50 is 1,500 naira and 50 kobo.

process_method.description: The raw, un-normalised value from your platform for how the transaction was processed.

is_reversal.description: Whether this transaction reverses an earlier one.

is_international_override.description: Whether the transaction crosses a border, when you want to override isInternational for this one variable.

is_triggered_by_user.description: Whether the user initiated the transaction directly, as opposed to the system or a schedule.

is_round_amount.description: Whether the amount is a round figure, for example 1,000, 5,000 or 10,000.

is_large_transaction.description: Whether the amount exceeds a limit set by the bank, customer or product.

counterparty.description: What you know about the counterparty that we cannot work out from the parties themselves.

code.description: The counterparty's industry or merchant category code.

is_linked_account.description: Whether the counterparty's account is linked to the sender's own profile.

is_new.description: Whether the entity has never used this counterparty before.

age_days.description: How long the counterparty relationship has existed, in days.

risk_tier.description: The risk score or tier you assigned the counterparty.

is_watchlisted.description: Whether the counterparty is on an internal or external watchlist.

device.description: The digital channel the transaction came through.

is_proxy.description: Whether the device's IP address appears to use a VPN, proxy or TOR.

ipAddress.description: The client's public IP address (IPv4 or IPv6).

geoCountry.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the device reports or the IP address maps to.

deviceFingerprint.description: A stable identifier for the device. It is compared with the entity's last login device.

accuracyM.description: How accurate the position is, in metres.

channelApp.description: The app or channel the customer used.

asset_type.description: The crypto asset, for example BTC, ETH, USDT, a stablecoin, a privacy coin or an NFT.

wallet_address.description: The origin or destination blockchain address.

travel_rule_complete.description: Whether the originator and beneficiary information the travel rule requires is complete.

mixer_exposure.description: Whether the wallet address has direct or indirect exposure to a mixer or tumbler.

sanctioned_address_exposure.description: Whether the wallet address has exposure to a sanctioned wallet, address or entity.

transactionReference.description: Your unique reference for this transaction. It identifies the transaction, not the event: the idempotency key is the event's externalEventId.

post.description:
One entry point for every event type. Send an event when something happens that your workflows should see, such as a payment, a login or a card action. **Triggering events start evaluations; every other event is accepted and stored.**

### Event types

Pick the request variant that matches `eventType`. Every field in the schema lists its type, whether it is required and what it means. Use the **Examples** selector to see a complete payload for each variant.

| Event | `eventType` | What it describes | Workflow type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Transaction | `transaction` | A payment, with its sender and beneficiaries in `data`. | Transaction Monitoring (TM) |
| Login | `account_activity` | A customer login. Carries `data.loginMethod`. | Transaction Monitoring (TM) |
| Card | `account_activity` | A card event. Carries `data.cardAction` (`created` or `updated`). | Transaction Monitoring (TM) |
| Onboarding | `onboarding` | A customer onboarding event. Carries `data.externalEntityId` (required) and `data.entityId` when the workflow is for an existing entity. | Customer Onboarding (CO) |

A login and a card event are both `account_activity`. Never send `loginMethod` and `cardAction` together. Pick the matching request variant below. The fields inside an onboarding event's `data` beyond the entity fields depend on the workflow you are running.

### Routing

- `transaction` and `account_activity` events carry an `eventCategory`. Every event runs the live TM workflows tagged with that category whose `eventTypes` includes the event's type. A TM workflow must list at least one event type to be saved or published.
- `onboarding` events are routed by `workflowId` and `workflowVersion`.
- `eventTypes` decides which events start a workflow, not what the workflow can read. Any TM workflow can use the `behavioural_insights.*` variables, including those learned from account activity.
- An `account_activity` event runs on `{ account_activity: data }`.

### Which statuses start an evaluation

| Event | Triggering `eventStatus` |
| --- | --- |
| Transaction | `acknowledged`, `pending` |
| Login | `attempted` |
| Card | `requested`, `activated`, `pin_changed` |
| Any kind | `processing` |

Any other status (for example `completed`, `successful`, `failed`, `issued`, `frozen`, `processed`) is stored without a run, and still updates the aggregates. Which statuses are allowed depends on the kind of event.

### Identifying the entity

There is no `externalEntityId` on the event itself. Each entity identifies itself inside `data`:

- On a `transaction`, the sender and each beneficiary carry their own `entityId` (the Youverify id) or their own `externalEntityId` (your id), with a `name` and `accountNumber`.
- On an `account_activity` event, the same fields sit at the root of `data`.
- `entityType` (`INDIVIDUAL` or `BUSINESS`) is required inside `data`: at the root of `data` for `account_activity` and `onboarding` events, and on the sender and each beneficiary of a `transaction`.

Send the `entityId` whenever you have it. We then skip resolving the entity from your `externalEntityId`, so the event is processed and enriched faster.

### Idempotency

`externalEventId` is the idempotency key. Sending the same `externalEventId` again returns the original evaluations with `replayed: true` and runs nothing. The repeat's payload is ignored even if it differs. An `externalEventId` with no live evaluation yet runs as normal. A transaction's `transactionReference` identifies the transaction, not the event.

### Lifecycle

An event has a `lifecycleId` only if you send one; we never generate it. An event without one is connected to no other event and adds nothing to session-risk counters. Send the same `lifecycleId` on related events, such as one session or one payment.
